learning_objective: 🎯 Master the physics of light! Learn how mirrors bounce light to form images and how lenses bend light to magnify the world.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Reflection is the bouncing back of light. Laws of Reflection: 1. Angle of Incidence = Angle of Reflection ($$ \angle i = \angle r $$). 2. Incident ray, reflected ray, and normal lie on the same plane.
Concave mirrors converge light (used in headlights, dentist mirrors). Convex mirrors diverge light and always form small, virtual images (used as rear-view mirrors in cars).

Refraction is the bending of light when it passes from one medium to another (e.g., air to glass) due to a change in speed. Snell's Law states: $$\frac{\sin i}{\sin r} = constant$$ (Refractive Index).
A Convex lens (thick in the middle) converges light rays and is a magnifying glass. A Concave lens (thin in the middle) diverges light rays.

Mirror Formula: $$\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$$. Lens Formula: $$\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$$. Magnification ($$m$$) tells us how much larger or smaller the image is compared to the object.

fun_activity.title: 🥄 The Spoon Mirror
fun_activity.instructions: Take a shiny stainless steel spoon. Look at the inner side (Concave); your face will look upside down! Now look at the outer bulging side (Convex); your face will be upright but smaller.

exam_tips: 📌 Sign Convention is crucial! Always take object distance ($$u$$) as negative.
📌 Power of a lens ($$P$$) = $$\frac{1}{f (in meters)}$$. Its SI unit is Dioptre (D).
📌 Practice drawing ray diagrams for Concave Mirrors and Convex Lenses (especially when the object is placed between F and 2F).
quick_recap: ⭐ Light travels fastest in a vacuum (3 × 10⁸ m/s).
⭐ A higher refractive index means the medium is denser and light travels slower in it.
⭐ Virtual images are always erect (upright), while real images are always inverted (upside down).
